bounded_reference: CVAT is used only as a role-separation reference: left task/tool, center spatial canvas, right selected-object context. The user explicitly rejects copying its visual density/style.

adopt.application: The Ankara map remains the primary spatial workspace and receives remaining width; a compact inspector cannot create a narrow persistent strip.
Setup, Propagation, Interference and other workflows remain in the left task drawer.
The selected cell/building/result sample gets contextual facts and direct actions without displacing the active tool.
Both task and inspector can be independently closed/collapsed to recover map space.
Keep selection highlight, map layer legend, entity identity and inspector facts synchronized.

reject.reason: A.T.O.M must preserve readable RF terminology, scientific evidence boundaries and operational clarity.

reject.lesson: Permanent dual panels at all widths
reject.reason: A.T.O.M map/cell interactions need real width; below desktop thresholds panels must overlay, replace or become a single sheet.
Map and RF states already have multiple semantic colors; use named controls and visible status text.
Do not add a general object browser, task queue or new navigation hierarchy to justify an inspector.
At 768 and 390, one sheet at a time is clearer and map-first than three narrow columns.

A_T_O_M_difference: A.T.O.M is a scientific planning instrument with explicit compute/freshness and a local-first workspace. The inspector is contextual spatial evidence, not a general object editor or production dashboard.
